_readme: UTAH CIVIL DEADLINE RULES -- 9 rows, URCP 12, 33, 34 and 36.
== THE ROW THAT IS NOT HERE: URCP 6(c)'s SEVEN-DAY MAIL EXTENSION =====
NO ROW IN THIS FILE CARRIES A `service_extension`, AND NONE MAY UNTIL THE
ENGINE CAN EXPRESS EXCLUSIVE-VS-COMBINED SERVICE. Held on Michael's
direction 2026-08-27, as an engine limitation with its own fix, not a
per-row workaround.
URCP 6(c): `When a party may or must act within a specified time after
service and service is made EXCLUSIVELY BY MAIL under Rule 5(b)(3)(C)(i),
7 days are added after the period would otherwise expire under paragraph
(a).` SEVEN, not three. Copying a neighbour's 3 would compute FOUR DAYS
EARLY on every mailed period.
But the trigger for it is not a method, it is an EXCLUSIVITY. This engine
carries ONE `service_method` field and `applies_when` is a method
allowlist, so it cannot say `by mail AND BY NOTHING ELSE`. A caller who
supplies `mail` for a party who was in fact served by mail AND e-mail
would get +7 and a date that is LATE -- by a week, in the direction that
loses a filing. Modelling it as `applies_when: ['mail']` would be exactly
the quiet wrongness this engine exists to avoid.
Tracked the way the service-COMPLETION mechanism was before Missouri: as
a real engine addition to be built deliberately, in its own pass. Until
then a mailed Utah period computes WITHOUT the seven days, which reports
EARLY -- safe, and disclosed rather than silent. See the open-work index.
== AND NO SERVICE-COMPLETION BLOCK, FOR THE OPPOSITE REASON ===========
URCP 5(b)(4): `Service by mail or electronic means is complete upon
sending.` No time-of-day condition, unlike Missouri's 5 p.m. rule or
Virginia's. `Complete upon sending` means the completion date IS the date
the caller already supplies, so a completion standard here would be a
mechanism that never moves anything -- dormant by construction. Omitted
deliberately, not overlooked.
sql/sairnlaw_deadline_calendars_utah.json covers 2026 AND NOTHING ELSE.
Utah Code 63G-1-301 is SUPERSEDED 1/1/2027; the successor moves Juneteenth
out of (1)(b)(ix) into (1)(a)(ii) and deletes its bespoke (2)(c)/(2)(d)
Monday rules, while URCP 6(a)(6)(E) still calls it `the third Monday of
June`. That shorthand is EXACTLY RIGHT for the current statute in every
year 2024-2032 (asserted by the generator, not assumed) and WRONG in eight
of the next nine from 1/1/2027 -- three days apart in 2027, rule 06-21 vs
statute 06-18. Encoding 06-21 would roll a deadline off a day that is not
a holiday: LATE.
So every 2027+ Utah computation refuses NOT_PROVISIONED on the engine's
own missing-year path. That is a HOLD, not a gap. DO NOT EXTEND THE
CALENDAR WITHOUT DECIDING WHETHER URCP 6(a)(6)(E) MEANS ITS OWN TEXT OR
THE STATUTE IT DESCRIBES.
== SOURCE, AND TWO TRAPS ON TOP OF IT ================================
Read verbatim 2026-08-27 from legacy.utcourts.gov, free and official on a
BARE curl -- no user-agent, no Accept header. Every rule page prints its
own `Effective:` date, so effective_from is REAL PER RULE here: 6 and 12
TRAP 1 -- THE HOST NAMED `legacy` IS THE CURRENT ONE. Every rule page
prints `Go to https://www.utcourts.gov/rules for current rules`, and that
URL 302s straight back to legacy.utcourts.gov/rules. legacy carries URCP
63 effective 2/13/2026, 58A 12/9/2025 and 45 11/1/2025. The hostname and
the banner are NOT a currency blocker -- same class as the mass.gov and
nccourts.gov 403s, where the scary signal means `not a browser`, never
`page absent`. www.utcourts.gov itself 406s to curl unless a user-agent
AND an Accept header are sent together; irrelevant, since legacy needs
neither.
TRAP 2, AND THIS ONE RUNS THE DANGEROUS WAY -- legacy returns HTTP 200
WITH AN ERROR-PAGE BODY for a rule that does not exist.
legacy.utcourts.gov/rules/urcp.html is 200 and 11,211 bytes of `We
couldn't find your page ... There was an error viewing this rule.` Every
other gated source announced absence with a 403, a 404 or a paywall. A
200 FROM THIS HOST IS NOT PROOF THE RULE IS THERE -- check the body.
== THE WEEKEND QUESTION ANSWERS ITSELF AT STEP ONE ====================
First jurisdiction seeded where it does. URCP 6(a)(1)(C) names both days
inside the rollover clause: `if the last day is a Saturday, Sunday, or
legal holiday, the period continues to run until the end of the next day
that is not a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday.` No holiday statute is
consulted for the weekend question at all, and there is no statewide-
coverage sub-question. isWeekend() is correct on the rule's own words.
== DAYS ARE DAYS, AND BACKWARD IS REAL ===============================
6(a)(1)(B) counts `every day, including intermediate Saturdays, Sundays,
and legal holidays`, so ut_urcp_6 declares NO short_period_exclusion_days
-- ABSENT, not 0. Six seeded states use 7 and three use 11; either would
push every short Utah deadline later than the rule provides.
6(a)(5) defines backward counting expressly, so rollover_suffix_backward
is a real citation rather than the blank NJ/NC/WA/MA/MO/WI carry. No
backward ROW is seeded even so.
== WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT SEEDED ===================================
(1) Any mailed-service row -- see the top of this readme.
(2) HOURS-BASED PERIODS. 6(a)(2) states periods in hours with its own
hour-granular rollover. This engine has calendar_days, business_days,
months and years, and no hours unit. A row here would be a real engine
addition, not a config change.
(3) 6(d)'s unrepresented-party rule -- for a party who is BOTH
unrepresented AND without an e-filing account, the period runs from the
SERVICE date rather than the FILING date. Keyed on party status, which
this engine has no field for. Omitting it reports EARLY.
(4) 6(e)'s inmate mailbox rule, and its `calculated from the date the
papers are received by the court` limb.
(5) Appellate rows, and the new Rules of Business and Chancery Court
Procedure.
(6) NO DEFENDANT FLOOR ON ANY DISCOVERY ROW -- searched 33, 34 and 36 for
`not be served`, `may not serve`, `after service of the summons` and
`commencement of the action`: ZERO hits each. Unlike Ohio and Indiana,
Utah's discovery periods run purely from service of the request, so no
designated_period shape applies. Reported as a searched-for absence.
== EARLY-DIRECTION GAPS IN THE CALENDAR, DISCLOSED ====================
URCP 6(a)(6) limb (M) (`any day designated by the Governor or
Legislature`) and Utah Code 63G-1-301(5) (governor's proclamations, up to
60 days and renewable) are ad hoc and not knowable in advance.
GOOD FRIDAY is the interesting one: 63G-1-301(1)(b)(iii) makes it a Utah
legal holiday -- on a WEEKDAY -- and 6(a)(6)'s thirteen limbs omit it.
Because 6(a)(6) says `means` rather than `includes`, the rule's list
should control and Good Friday should not roll a deadline; but limb (M)
could be read to sweep the statute back in, which would make the other
twelve limbs redundant. UNRESOLVED AND IT DOES NOT NEED RESOLVING:
omitting it can only report EARLY. Encoding it would be the risky choice.
Easter Sunday and the statute's `every Sunday` are already non-days under
6(a)(3)'s clerk's-office INACCESSIBILITY limb is likewise not modelled,
and it is safe because it is ADDITIONAL to the Saturday/Sunday/holiday
rollover rather than a replacement for it -- Minnesota's 6.01(a)(4) shape,
NOT Wisconsin's 801.15(1)(b). That distinction is what separates a
disclosable omission from a blocked jurisdiction.
URCP 4 (process) was NOT read, so what `service of the summons and
complaint` completes on -- and therefore what date a caller should supply
for the Rule 12 rows -- is not sourced from the rule text. The in-state /
out-of-state split below is taken from Rule 12's own words; Rule 4 may
define the boundary differently. Read it before relying on either row for
an out-of-state defendant.

rules.label: Answer after service of the summons and complaint WITHIN Utah

authority.quote: Unless otherwise provided by statute or order of the court, a defendant must file and serve an answer within 21 days after the service of the summons and complaint within the state and within 30 days after service of the summons and complaint outside the state.
authority.note: TWENTY-ONE DAYS FOR SERVICE WITHIN UTAH. The out-of-state limb is THIRTY and is a SEPARATE ROW with its own trigger, not a variant of this one -- the two are chosen by where service happened, which the caller knows and the engine cannot infer. NO SERVICE EXTENSION IS CARRIED: URCP 6(c) adds seven days for service made EXCLUSIVELY BY MAIL under Rule 5(b)(3)(C)(i), and this engine's single service_method field cannot express exclusivity, so applying it could report LATE by a week. A mailed period therefore computes EARLY here, disclosed rather than silent. URCP 4 was not read, so what 'service of the summons and complaint' completes on is not sourced from the rule text.

rules.label: Answer after service of the summons and complaint OUTSIDE Utah

authority.quote: Unless otherwise provided by statute or order of the court, a defendant must file and serve an answer within 21 days after the service of the summons and complaint within the state and within 30 days after service of the summons and complaint outside the state.
authority.note: THIRTY DAYS FOR SERVICE OUTSIDE UTAH, from the same sentence as the 21-day in-state limb. Seeded as its own row rather than as a variant because the choice between them turns on a fact -- where service was made -- that the caller supplies and the engine cannot derive from a date. Picking the wrong one of the two is a nine-day error, so the trigger names say 'in_state' and 'out_of_state' outright. NO SERVICE EXTENSION IS CARRIED; see the in-state row and the file readme.

authority.quote: A party served with a crossclaim must file and serve an answer to the crossclaim within 21 days after service.
authority.note: TWENTY-ONE DAYS, with NO in-state/out-of-state split -- the rule draws that distinction only for the summons and complaint. Do not infer a 30-day out-of-state limb here; the sentence does not provide one. NO SERVICE EXTENSION IS CARRIED; see the file readme.

authority.quote: The plaintiff must file and serve an answer to a counterclaim within 21 days after service of the counterclaim, unless the court orders otherwise.
authority.note: TWENTY-ONE DAYS. 'Unless the court orders otherwise' is a court-ordered override this engine cannot know about; a specific order always beats a seeded rule and the audit trail names the rule so a reader can tell. In a Rule 26.1 domestic-relations matter, Rule 12(a)(2) renames the parties -- plaintiff/petitioner, defendant/respondent, complaint/petition, counterclaim/counterpetition -- WITHOUT changing any period, so this row applies there under the other name. NO SERVICE EXTENSION IS CARRIED; see the file readme.

rules.label: Responsive pleading after a Rule 12 motion is denied or postponed to trial (Utah)

authority.quote: If the court denies the motion or postpones its disposition until the trial on the merits, the responsive pleading must be served within 14 days after notice of the court's action;
authority.note: FOURTEEN DAYS, AND THE PERIOD RUNS FROM NOTICE OF THE COURT'S ACTION -- not from the order's date, and not from the motion. Supply the date notice was given. This row REPLACES the 21- or 30-day period for the pleading it governs; Rule 12(a)(1) says the service of a Rule 12 motion 'alters these periods of time'. It is not a chain: one caller-supplied date produces one deadline. NOTE THE CARVE-OUT in the same sentence -- 'a motion directed to fewer than all of the claims in a pleading does not affect the time for responding to the remaining claims', so a partial motion leaves the original period running on the untouched claims and this row does not reach them. NO SERVICE EXTENSION IS CARRIED; see the file readme.

rules.label: Responsive pleading after service of a more definite statement (Utah)

authority.quote: If the court grants a motion for a more definite statement, the responsive pleading must be served within 14 days after the service of the more definite statement.
authority.note: FOURTEEN DAYS FROM SERVICE OF THE MORE DEFINITE STATEMENT ITSELF -- not from the order granting the motion. The distinction is the whole point of the limb: the order comes first and the statement follows, so a caller supplying the order's date computes EARLY. The same partial-motion carve-out noted on Rule 12(a)(1)(A) applies. NO SERVICE EXTENSION IS CARRIED; see the file readme.

authority.quote: The responding party shall serve a written response within 28 days after service of the interrogatories.
authority.note: TWENTY-EIGHT DAYS, matching Utah's other two discovery rules exactly -- 34(b)(2) and 36(c)(1) are both 28 as well, so this jurisdiction has no per-device variation to get wrong. NO DEFENDANT FLOOR: Rules 33, 34 and 36 were searched for 'not be served', 'may not serve', 'after service of the summons' and 'commencement of the action' and returned ZERO hits each, so unlike Ohio and Indiana there is no designated_period shape here. Reported as a searched-for absence, not an assumption. NO SERVICE EXTENSION IS CARRIED; see the file readme.

rules.label: Response to a request for production or inspection (Utah)

authority.quote: The responding party must serve a written response within 28 days after service of the request.
authority.note: TWENTY-EIGHT DAYS. Note this is the deadline for the WRITTEN RESPONSE, not for the production itself -- Rule 34(b)(2) has the responding party state that inspection will be permitted, and the request separately 'must specify a reasonable date, time, place, and manner of making the inspection'. That production date is chosen by the requesting party and is not computed here. NO DEFENDANT FLOOR (searched; see the Rule 33 row). NO SERVICE EXTENSION IS CARRIED; see the file readme.

rules.label: Response to requests for admission (Utah) — MISSING IT ADMITS THE MATTER

authority.quote: The matter is admitted unless, within 28 days after service of the request, the responding party serves upon the requesting party a written response.
authority.note: TWENTY-EIGHT DAYS, AND THE CONSEQUENCE OF MISSING IT IS AUTOMATIC ADMISSION -- the rule is phrased as 'the matter is admitted unless', not as a duty to respond. Utah requires the requesting party to print that warning on the request itself, in bold at the top right of the first page: 'You must respond to these requests for admissions within 28 days or the court will consider you to have admitted the truth of the matter as set forth in these requests.' Rule 36(b)(2) adds that failing to include the caution language 'may provide the non-requesting party with a basis under Rule 60(b) for excusable neglect to set aside any resulting order or judgment' -- so a defective request may be curable after the fact. That is a question of law, not arithmetic, and this row computes the date either way. NO DEFENDANT FLOOR (searched; see the Rule 33 row). NO SERVICE EXTENSION IS CARRIED; see the file readme.
